transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, well, I came in because for the past few weeks, I've just felt this... this heavy, sad pressure sitting on me. It's there almost all day. Even when I'm at work—I'm an LPN—and I'm smiling at my patients, inside I just feel like I'm barely holding myself together.
Has this heavy, sad feeling happened to you before, or is this the first time you've experienced something like this?
No, this is the first time. I've had bad days before, sure, but... nothing like this. It's never lasted this long or felt this constant.
Before these past few weeks, have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks where you felt persistently sad or depressed, even if it wasn't as severe as what you're experiencing now?

No, not really. I mean, I've had stressful weeks, especially with nursing, but never a full two weeks where I felt sad every single day. It's always just been a bad day or two and then I usually bounce back. So, no, I haven't had a period like that before.

During these past few weeks when you've been feeling this heavy sadness, have you noticed that things you normally enjoy doing—like hobbies, spending time with friends, or activities you usually find fun—don't seem as enjoyable or interesting to you anymore?

Yeah, I have. Usually, after my shifts, I'd paint or go to a yoga class, sometimes even salsa dancing just to decompress. But lately... I just go straight home and sit on the couch. I've even been ignoring texts from my friends. None of it really feels worth the effort right now.
Over these past few weeks, have you noticed any changes in your sleep? For example, are you sleeping more than usual, sleeping less, or having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Um, no, my sleep hasn't really changed. I mean, I'm tired when I get home from my shifts, but once I go to bed, I sleep fine. I haven't had any trouble falling asleep, and I'm not sleeping way more or less than usual. It's pretty much just my normal routine.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite over these past few weeks? Are you eating more, less, or about the same as usual?

Yeah, I'm eating quite a bit less. I know I should be eating regularly, especially right now, but... most days food just sounds completely unappealing. I'll actually realize halfway through a clinic shift that I've only had some crackers or a cup of coffee all day. I just don't have the desire to eat.
During these past few weeks, have you been feeling guilty about things, or have you been having thoughts that you're worthless or that things are your fault?

No, I wouldn't say I feel worthless or guilty. I mean, I feel bad that I'm not keeping up with my friends, but it's not this overwhelming guilt or anything. I don't feel like things are my fault, I just feel... flat, I guess. But not worthless.

Over these past few weeks, have you noticed any changes in how you move or act? For example, do you feel like you're moving or thinking more slowly than usual, or conversely, do you feel restless or like you need to keep moving?

Yeah, I have noticed that. Everything I do just feels slowed down right now. It's almost like I'm moving through syrup. Even simple things at the clinic, like gathering wound care supplies or finishing up my charting, they just take me noticeably longer than they should.
Over these past few weeks, have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions, or do you find your mind feeling foggy or scattered?

Yeah, definitely. My brain just feels really foggy lately. I actually find myself having to reread medication orders and wound-care notes a few times just to process what they say. And making decisions is hard right now... things I normally just do automatically at work, they make me freeze up, and I just end up second-guessing myself.
During these past few weeks, have you had any thoughts about death, or any thoughts that you or others would be better off if you weren't around?

Yeah. That’s actually what scared me enough to say something at my prenatal appointment. I’ve been having thoughts... well, just thoughts like I wish I wouldn't wake up. I don't have any actual plan to hurt myself or anything like that, but just having those kinds of thoughts really scared me.
You mentioned a prenatal appointment—are you currently pregnant?
Yes, I am. I'm currently pregnant.
When did you first notice these feelings of sadness and heaviness starting—was it before you became pregnant, or did it start after you found out you were pregnant?
It was definitely after I found out. Um, I'd say this has been going on for about three weeks now... it started just shortly after I learned I was pregnant.

Before you found out you were pregnant, in the weeks or months leading up to that discovery, were you experiencing any of these depressive feelings—the sadness, lack of interest in activities, or the slowed-down feeling—or did all of this start only after you learned you were pregnant?

No, none of that before. I was feeling perfectly fine in the months leading up to it. It really just... it only started after I learned I was pregnant. I didn't have any of the sadness or anything like that before then.

Have you ever had a period of several days or longer where you felt unusually energetic, needed very little sleep, your thoughts were racing, or you felt like you could do anything—almost the opposite of how you're feeling now?
No, I haven't. I've never really had a time where I felt like that... where I had all that extra energy or felt like I didn't need to sleep. It's never been like that for me.

Let me make sure I have this right—so far you've mentioned feeling persistently sad and heavy, losing interest in activities you normally enjoy, eating much less than usual, moving and thinking more slowly, having difficulty concentrating and making decisions, and having thoughts that you wish you wouldn't wake up. Have I captured all of the main changes you've noticed, or are there other significant changes in how you've been feeling or functioning that we haven't discussed yet?
Yeah, I think you've pretty much got it all. Um, I can't really think of anything else... that list pretty much sums up exactly what I've been going through these last few weeks.
